top_story: Iran’s 22 October threat to strike Gulf oil sites, undersea cables, datacentres, and AI facilities if the US or Israel attacks again widened the regional battlespace from military targets to the infrastructure that underpins daily life and Gulf economies. In the occupied West Bank, the 23 October killing of two Israeli soldiers triggered an Israeli punitive campaign in Hebron that quickly escalated by 24 October into the forced eviction of hundreds of Palestinian families, demolitions, and open displacement threats. Sudan shows the longer human trajectory of such coercive warfare: a year after the UAE-backed RSF seized El-Fasher, the city’s population has collapsed to roughly seven percent of last year’s peak amid killing, torture, and disappearances. The regional picture is one of conflict actors increasingly using collective punishment and infrastructure vulnerability to impose political pressure through civilian fear, displacement, and economic disruption.
